README.md.text:
# AI Governance Research Prototype

Research artifact / proof of concept for an Organization Science Stage 1 submission. Prepared 29 October 2026 from completed project outputs.

## Research overview

This artifact demonstrates an AI-enabled measurement pipeline for **disclosed evidence of implemented internal AI governance** in US public-company Form 10-K filings. It preserves the completed binary Governance v2 measurement and the frozen, inductively developed P01–P12 governance-practice coding. Original classifications, source identifiers, uncertainty states, prompts and execution records remain traceable.

The results are automated disclosure classifications. Independent human semantic validation remains pending. The artifact does not measure governance effectiveness or establish actual implementation dates.

## Data

The frame contains 1,500 companies from saved S&P 500 / MidCap 400 / SmallCap 600 constituent snapshots, observed over FY2020–FY2025: 9,000 potential firm-years. Item 1A and Item 7 are classified separately; the final analysis unit is CIK × fiscal year.

| Dataset | Complete coverage retained | Main file |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Final Governance v2 panel | 8,500 firm-years; 1,484 companies | [Governance panel](data/full_sample/governance/combined_firm_year_v2_panel.csv) |
| Double-unavailable exclusions | 500 firm-years, with blank binary labels | [Exclusion manifest](data/full_sample/governance/exclusion_manifest.csv) |
| Section exports | 9,000 records per section; 16,222 classified sections in total | `data/full_sample/governance/item*_v2_classification_results.csv` |
| Final Practices view | All 303 Governance-Positive firm-years; 184 companies | [Practices panel](data/full_sample/practices/firm_year_practices_panel.csv) |
| Practice evidence | All 403 evidence units; 606 supporting practice-label quotes | [Evidence](data/full_sample/practices/evidence_level_practices.csv), [quotes](data/full_sample/practices/practice_quotes.csv) |

Governance has 303 Positive and 8,197 Negative firm-years. Its delivered **observed-section OR** estimator includes 778 single-section observations: 17 Positive and 761 Negative. The `source_status` and section availability fields preserve this distinction. The frozen guideline also describes a stricter two-section negative rule; [methodology](docs/methodology.md) explains the documented estimator used by this delivery.

Practices contain 467 distinct firm-year–practice assignments. Of the 303 Positive firm-years, 281 have at least one assigned practice; 22 have no observed practice assignment. All 303 rows, including uncertainty and review flags, are retained. Governance-Negative and excluded firm-years were outside the practice-coding population.

## Measurement pipeline

1. Read saved, quality-screened complete Item 1A / Item 7 text and its source manifest. Binary v2 uses full section text without keyword screening.
2. Apply the saved v2 standard and complete prompt. Validate the response schema, evidence locations and exception states separately for each section.
3. Aggregate section labels using the original deterministic observed-section OR function. Preserve unavailable, unresolved and accession-conflict states.
4. For Governance-Positive observations, read the 403 existing evidence units and bounded same-chapter context blocks. Apply the frozen inductive codebook; union practice labels across evidence and sections within CIK × fiscal year.

The native practice workflow jointly coded practices, motivations and visions. Its original codebook, schema and native source outputs are retained as dependencies of exact P01–P12 reproduction. The primary practice views expose practice fields only. Separate Pro-AI Orientation, Governance Purpose and other research modules are excluded. A historical plotting file bearing “purpose” in its name supplies shared style functions only.

## Repository structure

```text
prototype/
├── README.md, requirements.txt
├── config/                 Frozen guidelines, full prompts, codebook and LLM snapshots
├── src/
│   ├── governance/         Final historical binary modules and their import dependencies
│   ├── practices/          Frozen native content-coding and aggregation modules
│   └── visualization/      Unmodified references for selected existing plots
├── scripts/                Supported offline verification and reproduction adapters
├── data/
│   ├── full_sample/        Complete Governance and Practices results
│   ├── reference/          Fixed size/GICS mapping and upstream source manifests
│   └── sample/             Five native section texts and existing outputs
├── outputs/
│   ├── summary_statistics/ Existing figure data and descriptive statistics
│   └── validation/         Run records, provenance and verification evidence
├── figures/                Ten curated original figures; PNG and existing PDF companions
└── docs/                   Methodology, dictionary, version audit and file provenance
```

Start with the [version audit](docs/version_audit.md), [data dictionary](docs/data_dictionary.md), [figure guide](docs/figures.md) and [source manifest](docs/source_manifest.csv). The source manifest distinguishes byte-identical copies from explicit row/column views and newly written documentation.

## Existing results

The selected Governance delivery is `implemented-internal-ai-governance-v2.0`, begun 13 October 2026. Its original manifest does not contain a standalone `run_id`; bundle identity, start timestamp and prompt version identify the run. Practices use `implemented-ai-governance-content-v1-20261018`, with the frozen codebook SHA-256 recorded in the native run manifest.

| Fiscal year | Eligible firm-years | Positive | Positive rate |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 2020 | 1,337 | 2 | 0.15% |
| 2021 | 1,394 | 2 | 0.14% |
| 2022 | 1,409 | 3 | 0.21% |
| 2023 | 1,441 | 35 | 2.43% |
| 2024 | 1,458 | 93 | 6.38% |
| 2025 | 1,461 | 168 | 11.50% |

The figure set covers annual Governance Positive rates, Positive-sample size and GICS composition, Size × Industry rates and 2023–2025 changes, practice distribution, annual practice prevalence and practice-assignment composition. Each figure's numerator, denominator, source version and original path are recorded in [figure_registry.csv](docs/figure_registry.csv).

## Reproducibility

Use Python 3.12; the verification environment used Python 3.12.14 and the exact package versions in `requirements.txt`. Run from this directory:

```powershell
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r requirements.txt
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -B scripts\verify.py
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -B scripts\reproduce.py --figures
```

The supported entry points work from the bundled files and block network calls and credential loading. `verify.py` reads the artifact and prints its checks. `reproduce.py` rebuilds the two firm-year panels and the exclusion panel; `--figures` replays the ten selected plots. Reproduced files go under `outputs/reproduced/`, leaving sealed results unchanged. A separate figure replay is available through `python -B scripts/plot_figures.py`.

An optional original-source comparison is `python -B scripts/verify.py --source-project ../ai-restrictions-concerns`. The original project is unnecessary for normal offline replay. See [reproducibility.md](docs/reproducibility.md) for validation evidence and the limits of historical entry points.

## Current limitations

- Human semantic accuracy, intercoder reliability and construct validity have not been established by these integrity checks. The inherited review queue contains 134 pending evidence records; 34 evidence units are uncodable and 77 carry a model review flag.
- Size and GICS metadata use a fixed snapshot retrieved on 19 September 2026, applied retrospectively to all years. Historical annual membership and market capitalization are not supplied.
- Complete upstream 10-K acquisition, extraction inputs and bulky API caches remain in the original project. Five full source sections and all practice context blocks are bundled. Fresh provider inference was not run, and exact future provider output is not established.
- This assembly preserves historical `temperature=0` requests with thinking and reasoning effort unspecified. It does not retrofit the shared client's later 25 October configuration.

All existing project files were read or copied only. No DeepSeek request, new classification, literature review or empirical analysis was performed during assembly.

# Guide to the selected figures

Ten original figures are retained as byte-identical copies. Existing PDF companions are included for six figures; the industry and Size × Industry source bundles supplied PNG only. The [machine-readable registry](figure_registry.csv) gives each original path, classification/visualization version, plotting function and statistic file.

Governance rates condition on eligible classified observations. Composition figures condition on Positive observations or on Practice assignments. These denominators answer different descriptive questions.

## 1. Annual Governance Positive rate

![Annual Governance Positive rate](../figures/governance/annual_positive_rate.png)

Scope: FY2020-FY2025. 8500 eligible firm-years; observed-section OR; single-section observations retained.

Numerator: Governance Positive firm-years. Denominator: All eligible classified firm-years in the fiscal year.

Data: `outputs/summary_statistics/governance/annual_trend_summary.csv`. Classification: `implemented-internal-ai-governance-v2.0`; visualization: `implemented-internal-ai-governance-v2.0`.

## 2. Firm-size composition within Governance Positive

![Firm-size composition within Governance Positive](../figures/governance/positive_size_composition.png)

Scope: FY2020-FY2025. 303 Positive firm-years; fixed S&P index size proxy.

Numerator: Positive firm-years in the size group and fiscal year. Denominator: All Governance Positive firm-years in that fiscal year.

Data: `outputs/summary_statistics/governance/size_composition.csv`. Classification: `implemented-internal-ai-governance-v2.0`; visualization: `firm_size_within_disclosure_composition_v1_20261026`.

## 3. GICS composition within Governance Positive

![GICS composition within Governance Positive](../figures/governance/positive_industry_composition.png)

Scope: FY2023-FY2025. 296 Positive firm-years in FY2023-FY2025; all 11 GICS Sectors.

Numerator: Positive firm-years in the GICS sector and fiscal year. Denominator: All Governance Positive firm-years in that fiscal year (35, 93, 168).

Data: `outputs/summary_statistics/governance/annual_industry_composition.csv`. Classification: `implemented-internal-ai-governance-v2.0`; visualization: `industry_within_disclosure_composition_v1_20261028`.

## 4. Annual Size x Industry Governance Positive rate

![Annual Size x Industry Governance Positive rate](../figures/governance/size_industry_annual_positive_rate.png)

Scope: FY2023-FY2025. 4360 classified firm-years; 99 annual size-sector cells; 296 Positive.

Numerator: Governance Positive firm-years within Year x Size x GICS Sector. Denominator: Valid binary firm-years within the same cell.

Data: `outputs/summary_statistics/governance/size_industry/year_size_sector_statistics.csv`. Classification: `implemented-internal-ai-governance-v2.0`; visualization: `governance_size_industry_v1_20261028`.

## 5. Change in Size x Industry Governance Positive rates

![Change in Size x Industry Governance Positive rates](../figures/governance/size_industry_change_2023_2025.png)

Scope: FY2023 to FY2025. 33 size-sector cells; source small-N and sparse-Positive flags retained.

Numerator: Difference between the two existing cell rates. Denominator: Each endpoint has its own valid classified cell denominator.

Data: `outputs/summary_statistics/governance/size_industry/rate_changes.csv`. Classification: `implemented-internal-ai-governance-v2.0`; visualization: `governance_size_industry_v1_20261028`.

## 6. Pooled Size x Industry Governance Positive rate

![Pooled Size x Industry Governance Positive rate](../figures/governance/size_industry_pooled_positive_rate.png)

Scope: FY2023-FY2025 pooled. 4360 firm-year observations; 33 pooled cells; repeated firms across years count as firm-years.

Numerator: Sum of Positive firm-years in the size-sector cell over the three years. Denominator: Sum of valid classified firm-years in that cell over the three years.

Data: `outputs/summary_statistics/governance/size_industry/pooled_statistics.csv`. Classification: `implemented-internal-ai-governance-v2.0`; visualization: `governance_size_industry_v1_20261028`.

## 7. Distribution of disclosed governance practices

![Distribution of disclosed governance practices](../figures/practices/practice_distribution.png)

Scope: FY2020-FY2025. All 12 practices; 467 assignments; multi-label; zero-assignment and review cases retained in denominator.

Numerator: Positive firm-years assigned a Practice ID; deduplicated across evidence and sections. Denominator: All 303 Governance Positive firm-years.

Data: `outputs/summary_statistics/practices/practice_category_statistics.csv [scope=all]`. Classification: `implemented-ai-governance-content-v1.0`; visualization: `implemented-ai-governance-content-v1-20261018`.

## 8. Practice prevalence within annual Governance Positive samples

![Practice prevalence within annual Governance Positive samples](../figures/practices/practice_annual_prevalence.png)

Scope: FY2020-FY2025. 72 year-practice cells; multi-label; early years have only 2-3 Positive observations.

Numerator: Distinct annual Positive firm-years assigned the Practice ID. Denominator: All Governance Positive firm-years in that fiscal year (2, 2, 3, 35, 93, 168).

Data: `outputs/summary_statistics/practices/practice_category_statistics.csv [scope=fiscal_year]`. Classification: `implemented-ai-governance-content-v1.0`; visualization: `implemented-ai-governance-content-v1-20261018`.

## 9. Annual composition of Practice assignments

![Annual composition of Practice assignments](../figures/practices/practice_annual_assignment_share.png)

Scope: FY2020-FY2025; emphasis FY2023-FY2025. All 303 Positive firm-years; 467 assignments; 22 zero-assignment firm-years contribute no assignments.

Numerator: Distinct annual firm-year assignments to the Practice ID. Denominator: Annual sum of assignments over all 12 practices: 5, 5, 6, 54, 135, 262.

Data: `outputs/summary_statistics/practices/annual_practice_composition.csv; annual_assignment_totals.csv`. Classification: `implemented-ai-governance-content-v1.0`; visualization: `implemented-ai-governance-content-v1-20261018`.

## 10. Annual counts of Practice assignments

![Annual counts of Practice assignments](../figures/practices/practice_annual_assignment_count.png)

Scope: FY2020-FY2025; emphasis FY2023-FY2025. All 12 practices; annual assignment totals 5, 5, 6, 54, 135, 262.

Numerator: Distinct annual firm-year assignments to each Practice ID. Denominator: No percentage denominator; bar height is annual total assignments, not unique firm-years.

Data: `outputs/summary_statistics/practices/annual_practice_composition.csv; annual_assignment_totals.csv`. Classification: `implemented-ai-governance-content-v1.0`; visualization: `implemented-ai-governance-content-v1-20261018`.

## Interpretation and selection

The binary annual trend and original Practice frequency/prevalence plots remain valid despite their earlier rendering date: later figures cite the same unchanged final datasets. The newer Practice composition plots use assignment shares, while the annual prevalence heatmap uses Positive firm-years. The three Size × Industry figures retain annual levels, endpoint changes and pooled levels as complementary views.

Size/GICS membership is the fixed 19 September 2026 retrieval snapshot. Early FY2020–FY2022 Positive counts are only 2, 2 and 3. All plots describe model-coded observed disclosure, with human semantic validation pending.

Portable replay uses the existing plot functions and supplied statistics. The assembly reproduced all ten selected PNGs byte for byte; evidence is retained in `outputs/validation/figure_reproduction.json`.

# Reproduction status and supported execution

All commands below run from the prototype root. They use paths resolved from the script location and require no original-project directory for normal replay. The original full-sample model outputs remain unchanged.

## Verified offline functions

`python -B scripts/verify.py` checks sealed/copy hashes, rebuilds the 8,500-row Governance panel and 500-row exclusion panel through the original final `aggregate` function, and compares all 29 fields per row. It also reconstructs the original 303-row native content panel through its original union function and compares all 108 native fields, then checks the 28-field primary Practice view. All 403 native evidence results pass the original structural/category/status/context-quote validator; all 606 Practice quote rows match their stored locations.

Five native section examples cover one Negative, four Positive sections, early-year evidence, a concrete legal/security review, and a firm-year Positive in both chapters. Their source hashes, schema/evidence validation and complete system prompt are checked without inference. Historical request bodies are assembled locally; no response is generated. These examples provide an execution smoke test and are not an accuracy evaluation set.

All five binary request-body hashes match the original section exports. One original saved Practice request also matches the frozen runtime builder and hash exactly. That check resolves the extra trailing instruction in the saved readable Practice template; the exact runtime scaffold is stored separately, leaving the original snapshot unchanged.

`python -B scripts/reproduce.py` writes rebuilt Governance, exclusion and Practice panels under `outputs/reproduced/`. Adding `--figures` replays all ten curated figures. `python -B scripts/plot_figures.py` runs just the figure replay. The figure replay report compares the resulting PNG bytes and pixels with the selected original assets. The assembly environment reproduced all ten PNGs byte for byte. Exact rendering on another operating system or package version has not been established.

The original figures are copied unchanged into `figures/`. Replay outputs remain separate. `outputs/validation/figure_reproduction.json` retains the assembly's rendering comparison, and `prototype_validation.json` retains the deterministic checks. The original-project audit additionally checked all 306 Positive source text hashes and the evidence/quote locations against those full texts; only five full texts are bundled.

Temporary replay outputs and the relocation-test copy were removed after their verification reports were retained. Historical generated paths in those reports describe the check location; running the supported commands recreates replay outputs under `outputs/reproduced/`.

## Why adapters are needed

The historical modules assume their original repository layout and combine measurement with execution/report writers. The supported adapter imports the unmodified copied modules under separate package namespaces, supplies relocated paths and calls their pure validation/aggregation functions. It blocks network connections, transports, inference functions and credential loading.

Historical visualization modules also resolve old paths at import time and contain plots for unrelated projects. The figure adapter compiles explicitly named copied function definitions and binds local data paths and shared style functions. The source definitions and their hashes are recorded in the replay report. The original content renderer is limited to its existing Practice frequency and annual-prevalence blocks; its practice plotting expressions are preserved. No categories, labels, denominator rules or visual encodings are redesigned.

Unchanged shared plotting reference files can contain unused branches for other disclosure variables. The portable adapter executes only Governance, Practice and shared-style definitions; it does not load separate Orientation or Purpose datasets or classifier modules.

`src/governance/reference_entrypoints/` and `src/practices/reference_entrypoints/` preserve original orchestration for inspection. Their original package/layout assumptions and external data dependencies prevent direct standalone execution from their relocated archival paths. The supported portable commands are the scripts above.

## Environment

The assembly reused the existing project environment: Python 3.12.14, matplotlib 3.11.2, numpy 2.5.3, Pillow 12.3.0 and PyYAML 6.0.3. Exact versions are pinned in `requirements.txt`. A clean environment installation and non-Windows rendering were not performed. Standard-library CSV/JSON operations preserve identifiers as strings; no pandas dependency is needed by the supported scripts.

## External or unverified functions

| Function | Status / prerequisites |
| --- | --- |
| Saved-result checks and deterministic aggregation | Verified from bundled complete classifications |
| Practice schema/context-quote validation | Verified for all 403 evidence results from bundled inputs |
| Sample binary validation and historical request assembly | Verified for five bundled section texts |
| Selected plot replay | Verified; all ten PNGs match the original bytes in the recorded environment |
| Full-universe source TXT hash recheck | Full original files required; the assembly checked all Positive sources, and source existence for all 16,222 valid inputs |
| Upstream acquisition / full extraction | Not rerun; complete upstream corpora, extraction state and original environment required |
| Historical cache-based original `report` stages | Bulky caches and original layout required; portable replay uses saved section/evidence exports instead |
| Fresh binary or Practice inference | Not executed; requires separate authorization, complete inputs, compatible historical configuration and provider access |
| Human semantic validation / accuracy | Pending; no human decisions or reliability statistic created |

The original binary `prepare` stage additionally depends on the upstream secondary-QA table `outputs/full_universe_item1a/secondary_qa/secondary_qa_results.csv`, the repair comparison `data/interim/documents/item1a_review_repair_20260930_v3/comparison.csv`, and the baseline settings manifest `data/interim/classifications/full_universe_item7_implemented_internal_ai_governance/v1/run_manifest.json`, alongside the source manifests and full section texts. The original reporting stages require their cache, request/response, protection and pilot state. Practice `prepare` also reads the original binary evidence-context bundle; portable replay instead includes its already prepared 403 evidence units. These external stages were preserved for inspection and were not executed.

The original request-log hashes and compact complete failure/error event views are bundled. Full requests, responses, cache state and original execution logs remain in the source project. Original historical failure events are preserved separately from zero final classification failures. No secret keys, `.env` files or credentials are required by the supported offline entry points.

## Provenance checks and maintenance

Use `python -B scripts/verify.py --source-project PATH_TO_ORIGINAL_PROJECT` for an optional read-only check of original source hashes. Without this option, the prototype checks only its bundled inputs and sealed files and remains portable.

`scripts/assemble_from_project.py` documents the one-time copy/view assembly and refuses to overwrite existing destinations. `scripts/finalize_bundle.py` creates the source manifest and seals the finished artifact after documentation and validation. These are assembly tools; they are unnecessary for routine reviewer replay. Temporary replay outputs, local environments and caches are excluded from the sealed deliverable inventory.

# Version and source audit

Audit date: 29 October 2026. The audit preceded copying. Selection used run records, frozen standards, code/configuration hashes, completed coverage and downstream input hashes. File modification times were not used to rank versions.

## Selected binary delivery

| Attribute | Audited value |
| --- | --- |
| Original bundle | `outputs/full_universe_implemented_internal_ai_governance_v2/` |
| Prompt / classification version | `implemented-internal-ai-governance-v2.0` |
| Recorded start | `2026-10-13T08:45:17.873118+00:00` |
| Recorded standalone Run ID | Absent from the original manifest; no synthetic value inserted into the data |
| Completion evidence | Run status complete; delivery status complete; delivery QA passed |
| Main result | `combined_firm_year_v2_panel.csv`, SHA-256 `dc4b64256cbf72caf5c7bc425fc5daeacf36896b59f2109af97976c6d0237849` |
| Final coverage | 8,500 classified firm-years, 500 separate exclusions; 303 Positive, 8,197 Negative; 16,222 classified sections |
| Main + recovery prompt versions | 16,143 main, 56 recovery-1, 23 recovery-2 classified sections |

The final panel is the firm-year result. Section exports are retained as inputs and evidence rather than substituted for the panel. The saved delivery manifest covers 18 artifacts, all of whose current hashes match. Later Governance figures cite this same panel hash.

### Historical code lineage

The run bundle's `code_snapshot/governance_v2.py` is an execution-stage snapshot, hash `3ae1a27f...15844f`. Subsequent recovery and final delivery changed the final aggregation/QA code. The final delivery manifest explicitly records final code hashes:

| Module | Final delivery SHA-256 |
| --- | --- |
| `governance_v2.py` | `6d3f4da867dcb5d365b6558a16c9d45534bea126a082c0de0718d605632f30ad` |
| `governance_v2_recovery.py` | `f68a82f05d0ccc98c9b5286e03ee8bec8216ac26d702ff4b503463f4a6cbf259` |
| `governance_v2_delivery.py` | `1fb6c3a605053a9592ff7d5cc19463f596623c134673cc292f0a5163df3aef9b` |

The copies in `tmp/deepseek_global_config_20261025/before/src/ai_restrictions/` match all three hashes. They are therefore the selected final historical modules. The historical client and prompt come from the original run snapshot; supporting imports come from the pre-update source snapshot. The portable adapter supplies relocated paths and validates the final aggregate against the entire saved panel.

The live shared client was changed on 25 October to explicit enabled thinking and high reasoning effort, omitting temperature. Using that client would misdescribe this completed historical run. Separate historical clients and saved configurations preserve the actual request parameters.

## Selected Practices delivery

| Attribute | Audited value |
| --- | --- |
| Original bundle | `outputs/implemented_ai_governance_content_analysis/` |
| Recorded Run ID | `implemented-ai-governance-content-v1-20261018` |
| Prompt version | `implemented-ai-governance-content-v1.0` |
| State directory | `data/interim/classifications/implemented_ai_governance_content_analysis/v1/` |
| Frozen time | `2026-10-18T08:01:47.017110+00:00` |
| Codebook SHA-256 | `eb145750b1b3169aa1c372395d1810cbe0ff9008175325f261bd39b58753a698` |
| Native firm-year result SHA-256 | `3f13876a0144b85509efdd0d0e7fbec7606161f7acbc7f4ef11d02e9b7909253` |
| Coverage | All 303 binary Positive firm-years; 403 evidence units; 12 practice categories |
| Validation status | Automatic integrity passed; human semantic validation pending |

All 81 original delivery-manifest file hashes match. The native code snapshot matches the manifest, including the core content-coding module, reporting module, client and prompt. The primary Practices CSV is an explicit column projection of the native final panel and retains all 303 rows. Native joint outputs are retained unchanged to reproduce the original aggregation and schema checks.

The 26 October Practice visualization uses this same frozen run and codebook. Its annual assignment-composition statistics do not constitute a new classification version. No later completed, separately validated P01–P12 classification superseding this frozen run was identified in the audited project.

### Saved template versus actual runtime message

The Practice bundle's saved `user_prompt_template.txt` appends `Return the required JSON for this evidence_id.` after the evidence object. The frozen `closed_coding` implementation assembles the user message inline and omits that last line. An original saved request confirms the inline implementation. The artifact preserves the snapshot unchanged, adds the exact runtime scaffold and retry suffix extracted from source, and includes a byte-identical original request. The actual payload SHA-256 is `8b0388e78c5169366d8051902fb0300e038b71e684d01f806effa0bdd81e65ce`. This documentation discrepancy is resolved explicitly; the templates are not silently treated as identical. See `outputs/validation/prompt_rendering_audit.json`.

## Other versions and excluded material

| Existing material | Treatment and reason |
| --- | --- |
| Fixed-sample implemented-governance v1 and full-universe v1 | Earlier definition/pipeline; superseded for this binary measurement. Classification data and old subtype charts excluded. Small legacy modules remain only where required by the frozen v2 import graph. |
| Item 7 implemented-governance v1 | Earlier section-only measurement. Its run metadata was the historical configuration source; its labels are not merged into v2. |
| G1/G2/G3/R1/R2 subtype visualizations | Incompatible with the binary-v2 construct and P01–P12 inductive practices; excluded. |
| Preliminary open-coding labels and draft codebooks | Development history; excluded from final classifications. The development sample, frozen method, refinement audit and final prompts preserve relevant lineage. |
| Pro-AI Orientation, Governance Purpose, temporal/adoption/position analyses | Outside this artifact's measurement scope; their datasets and analytical modules excluded. |
| 28 October size/industry pie variants | Same source measurement; the selected stacked bars provide a compact comparison. Reformatting did not supersede their data. |
| Bulky caches, raw API responses and complete request payloads | Remain in the original project. Final successes, complete failure-event views, original log hashes, recovery records and accounting are bundled. |

## Figure lineage and checks

The selected figures draw from binary v2 and the frozen Practice run only. Four downstream visualization manifests have matching classification-source hashes. Independent recalculation matched 18 size-composition cells, 33 industry-composition cells, 99 Size × Industry cells, 84 Practice prevalence cells and 72 Practice assignment-composition cells. The latter count distinct firm-year–practice assignments.

The original 18 October frequency and annual-prevalence figures remain valid because their underlying classification was unchanged. The 26 October assignment-composition figures add a different denominator; they do not replace prevalence. Three complementary 28 October Size × Industry figures retain annual rates, endpoint changes and pooled rates.

## Recorded issues and handling

1. **Coverage estimator differs from the guideline's strict default.** The source workflow explicitly adopts observed-section OR. All delivered labels are preserved; 761 single-section negatives are marked by coverage fields and discussed prominently.
2. **No standalone binary Run ID field.** The manifest retains this absence. Bundle identity, recorded start, prompt version and file hashes jointly identify the selected run.
3. **Human semantic validation remains open.** The Practices run has 134 pending evidence records. No current project review database was found at its configured path during audit; the copied panel records every firm-year as `not_reviewed`.
4. **Shared native Practice schema.** Three-dimensional native material is an unavoidable dependency of the existing validator and union function. P01–P12 views and selected figures define the artifact's research scope; later Purpose modules are absent.
5. **External full-source and API state.** Five native text sections and all bounded Practice contexts are included. Full text acquisition/extraction and fresh paid inference were not reproduced.
6. **Fixed metadata timing.** Size/GICS labels use the 19 September 2026 retrieval snapshot retrospectively. The snapshot supplies no annual historical membership or effective-date series.
7. **Practice user-template snapshot differs from runtime assembly.** Both are retained, with an exact saved request and original code establishing the runtime message. The source snapshot is not overwritten.

There is no unresolved file-hash conflict in the selected final datasets. These substantive scope and validation limits remain explicit in the artifact. Machine-readable evidence is in `outputs/validation/project_audit_20261029.json`, `figure_audit_20261029.json`, original run records and the final source manifest.

"""Replay selected existing figures with unchanged plotting functions and local data.

Historical plotting modules combine several projects and resolve old repository
paths at import time. We compile only the named, copied function definitions,
then bind their data paths and shared style explicitly. The original source files
remain byte-identical. The joint content figure function is restricted to its
existing practice-frequency and annual-practice blocks, as documented below.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import ast
import copy
import csv
import hashlib
import json
import math
import os
import textwrap
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace

from _prototype import (ROOT, PDATA, PIDS, load_frozen, read_csv, read_json,
                        replay_output, require, sha, write_json)

REFERENCE = ROOT / "src/visualization/reference"
EXTRACTIONS = []


def selected_definitions(path, names, bindings, practice_blocks_only=False):
    """Load explicitly named definitions; do not execute historical module setup."""
    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig")
    tree = ast.parse(text)
    chosen = []
    found = set()
    for node in tree.body:
        node_names = ({node.name} if isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.ClassDef)) else
                      {x.id for x in node.targets if isinstance(x, ast.Name)} if isinstance(node, ast.Assign) else set())
        if not (node_names & set(names)):
            continue
        found |= node_names & set(names)
        source_hash = hashlib.sha256(ast.get_source_segment(text, node).encode()).hexdigest()
        EXTRACTIONS.append(dict(source=path.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix(), definitions=sorted(node_names & set(names)),
                                source_definition_sha256=source_hash,
                                selection="practice blocks only" if practice_blocks_only else "verbatim definition; paths bound by adapter"))
        node = copy.deepcopy(node)
        if practice_blocks_only:
            body = []
            for statement in node.body:
                # Everything from practice co-occurrence onward belongs to unselected figures.
                if isinstance(statement, ast.Assign) and any(isinstance(x, ast.Name) and x.id == "co" for x in statement.targets):
                    break
                # The original three-dimension loop is restricted to its first, practice tuple.
                if isinstance(statement, ast.For) and isinstance(statement.target, ast.Tuple):
                    if [x.id for x in statement.target.elts if isinstance(x, ast.Name)] == ["dim", "name", "title"]:
                        statement.iter.elts = statement.iter.elts[:1]
                body.append(statement)
            node.body = body
        chosen.append(node)
    require(set(names) <= found, "Missing copied plotting definition: " + repr(set(names) - found))
    namespace = dict(bindings)
    module = ast.fix_missing_locations(ast.Module(body=chosen, type_ignores=[]))
    exec(compile(module, str(path), "exec"), namespace)
    return SimpleNamespace(**{name: namespace[name] for name in names})


def typed_table(path):
    def cast(value):
        if value == "":
            return None
        if value in ["True", "False"]:
            return value == "True"
        try:
            return int(value)
        except ValueError:
            try:
                return float(value)
            except ValueError:
                return value
    return [{k: cast(v) for k, v in row.items()} for row in read_csv(path)]


def replay_figures(output):
    output = Path(output).resolve()
    require(output.is_relative_to(ROOT / "outputs/reproduced"), "Figure replay must remain within outputs/reproduced")
    output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    os.environ["MPLCONFIGDIR"] = str(output / "_matplotlib_cache")
    import matplotlib
    from PIL import Image, ImageChops
    EXTRACTIONS.clear()
    matplotlib.use("Agg")

    common = dict(ROOT=ROOT, Path=Path, os=os, json=json, csv=csv, textwrap=textwrap,
                  math=math, Counter=Counter, defaultdict=defaultdict, require=require)
    style = selected_definitions(REFERENCE / "purpose_plot_style.py",
                                 ["PALETTE", "NAVY", "rows", "sha", "read", "csvout", "check", "wrap", "configure", "title", "footer", "grid", "save", "legend_axis"], common)
    base_defs = selected_definitions(REFERENCE / "firm_size_disclosure.py", ["SIZE_COLORS", "SIZES", "YEARS", "save_figure"], common)
    base = SimpleNamespace(style=style, save_figure=base_defs.save_figure, SIZE_COLORS=base_defs.SIZE_COLORS,
                           SIZES=base_defs.SIZES, YEARS=base_defs.YEARS)
    expected = {}
    audits = {}
    stats = ROOT / "outputs/summary_statistics"

    # Governance trend: unchanged historical renderer and saved annual statistics.
    matplotlib.rcdefaults()
    trend = output / "governance/trend"
    trend.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    governance = load_frozen("governance")
    governance.OUT = trend
    annual = typed_table(stats / "governance/annual_trend_summary.csv")
    governance.figures(annual)
    expected["figures/governance/annual_positive_rate.png"] = trend / "figures/figure1_annual_positive_rate.png"

    # Size composition: the original function receives the Governance target only.
    matplotlib.rcdefaults()
    size = output / "governance/size"
    size.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    bindings = dict(common, base=base, FIGURES=size, TABLES=stats / "governance", YEARS=base.YEARS, SIZES=base.SIZES,
                    TARGETS={"governance_positive": ("governance", "Positive")},
                    TITLES={"governance_positive": "Firm-Size Composition among Firms with Implemented AI Governance"},
                    read=lambda path: read_csv(stats / "governance/size_composition.csv"))
    renderer = selected_definitions(REFERENCE / "firm_size_target_composition.py", ["plot_compositions"], bindings)
    audits["size_composition"] = renderer.plot_compositions()
    expected["figures/governance/positive_size_composition.png"] = size / "figure01_governance_positive_firm_size_composition.png"

    # Industry composition: same 11 codes, colors and conditional denominator.
    matplotlib.rcdefaults()
    industry = output / "governance/industry"
    industry.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    sector_rows = read_csv(ROOT / "data/reference/gics_sector_mapping.csv")
    sectors = {x["gics_sector_code"]: x["gics_sector"] for x in sector_rows}
    colors = {x["gics_sector_code"]: x["color"] for x in sector_rows}
    bindings = dict(common, base=base, OUT=industry, YEARS=(2023, 2024, 2025), SECTORS=sectors, COLORS=colors,
                    TARGETS={"governance_positive": ("governance", "Positive")},
                    read=lambda path: read_csv(stats / "governance/annual_industry_composition.csv"),
                    dump=lambda path, value: write_json(path, value))
    renderer = selected_definitions(REFERENCE / "industry_target_composition.py", ["plots"], bindings)
    audits["industry_composition"] = renderer.plots()
    expected["figures/governance/positive_industry_composition.png"] = industry / "figure01_governance_positive_industry_composition.png"

    # Three complementary Size x Industry figures; all original cell flags retained.
    matplotlib.rcdefaults()
    cross = output / "governance/size_industry"
    cross.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    bindings = dict(common, base=base, FIGURES=cross, REPORT=cross, YEARS=(2023, 2024, 2025), SIZES=base.SIZES,
                    SECTORS=list(sectors.values()), SMALL_N=20, SPARSE_P=5,
                    dump=lambda path, value: write_json(path, value))
    renderer = selected_definitions(REFERENCE / "governance_size_industry.py", ["plot_figures"], bindings)
    tab = stats / "governance/size_industry"
    audits["size_industry"] = renderer.plot_figures(typed_table(tab / "year_size_sector_statistics.csv"),
                                                   typed_table(tab / "pooled_statistics.csv"), typed_table(tab / "rate_changes.csv"))
    for original, slug in [("figure1_annual_positive_rate", "size_industry_annual_positive_rate"),
                           ("figure2_rate_change_2023_2025", "size_industry_change_2023_2025"),
                           ("figure3_pooled_positive_rate", "size_industry_pooled_positive_rate")]:
        expected[f"figures/governance/{slug}.png"] = cross / (original + ".png")

    # Original content renderer restricted to its existing practice-only blocks.
    matplotlib.rcdefaults()
    content = output / "practices/content"
    content.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    p, reporting = load_frozen("practices")
    p.OUT = content
    panel = read_json(PDATA / "native/evidence_level_coding.json")
    units = read_json(PDATA / "native/evidence_units.json")
    book = read_json(ROOT / "config/practices_prompts/codebook.json")
    native_panel = reporting.aggregate(units, {e["evidence_id"]: e for e in panel}, book)
    practice_book = dict(book, categories=[c for c in book["categories"] if c["dimension"] == "practices"])
    renderer = selected_definitions(ROOT / "src/practices/ai_restrictions/governance_content_reporting.py", ["figures"], dict(common, g=p), practice_blocks_only=True)
    renderer.figures(practice_book, native_panel, [], [], [])
    expected["figures/practices/practice_distribution.png"] = content / "figures/01_practices_frequency.png"
    expected["figures/practices/practice_annual_prevalence.png"] = content / "figures/04_practices_by_year.png"

    # Original 20261026 assignment-composition renderer, supplied from native P01-P12 counts.
    matplotlib.rcdefaults()
    composition = output / "practices/annual"
    composition.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    themes = {c["id"]: c["name"] for c in practice_book["categories"]}
    freq = {t: sum(row[t] for row in native_panel) for t in themes}
    order = sorted(themes, key=lambda t: (-freq[t], t))
    years = list(range(2020, 2026))
    annual = []
    for year in years:
        ps = [row for row in native_panel if row["fiscal_year"] == year]
        counts = {t: sum(row[t] for row in ps) for t in themes}
        annual.append(dict(fiscal_year=year, positive_firm_year_n=len(ps), assigned_firm_year_n=sum(any(row[t] for t in themes) for row in ps), counts=counts, assignments=sum(counts.values())))
    data = dict(themes=themes, order=order, years=years, annual=annual, panel=native_panel, assignment_n=sum(freq.values()))
    renderer = selected_definitions(REFERENCE / "plot_governance_practices.py", ["figures"], dict(common, style=style, check=require))
    audits["practice_composition"] = renderer.figures(data, composition)
    expected["figures/practices/practice_annual_assignment_share.png"] = composition / "annual_governance_practices_composition_share.png"
    expected["figures/practices/practice_annual_assignment_count.png"] = composition / "annual_governance_practices_composition_count.png"

    comparisons = []
    for original, recreated in expected.items():
        with Image.open(ROOT / original) as a, Image.open(recreated) as b:
            equal_pixels = a.size == b.size and ImageChops.difference(a.convert("RGB"), b.convert("RGB")).getbbox() is None
        comparisons.append(dict(prototype_figure=original, replay_path=recreated.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix(),
                                original_sha256=sha(ROOT / original), replay_sha256=sha(recreated),
                                equal_png_bytes=sha(ROOT / original) == sha(recreated), equal_rgb_pixels=equal_pixels))
    require(len(comparisons) == 10, "Selected figure coverage differs")
    report = dict(llm_calls=0, selected_figures_replayed=10,
                  byte_identical_png_n=sum(x["equal_png_bytes"] for x in comparisons),
                  pixel_identical_png_n=sum(x["equal_rgb_pixels"] for x in comparisons),
                  comparisons=comparisons, original_function_extractions=EXTRACTIONS,
                  renderer_checks=audits, runtime=dict(matplotlib=matplotlib.__version__),
                  scope="Saved data and original plotting functions; no inference or new empirical analysis")
    write_json(output / "figure_replay_report.json", report)
    return report


if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--output-dir", default="outputs/reproduced/figures")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    report = replay_figures(replay_output(args.output_dir))
    print(json.dumps({k: report[k] for k in ["llm_calls", "selected_figures_replayed", "byte_identical_png_n", "pixel_identical_png_n"]}, indent=2))

"""Rebuild the delivered firm-year panels from saved section/evidence classifications."""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json

from _prototype import (GDATA, PDATA, copied_file_integrity, fields, governance_replay,
                        practices_replay, replay_output, sealed_file_integrity, write_csv, write_json)


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--output-dir", default="outputs/reproduced")
    parser.add_argument("--figures", action="store_true", help="Also replay all ten selected existing figures")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    sealed_file_integrity()
    copied_file_integrity()
    output = replay_output(args.output_dir)
    panel, exclusions, governance = governance_replay()
    practices, practice_checks = practices_replay()
    write_csv(output / "governance/combined_firm_year_v2_panel.csv", panel, fields(GDATA / "combined_firm_year_v2_panel.csv"))
    write_csv(output / "governance/exclusion_manifest.csv", exclusions, fields(GDATA / "exclusion_manifest.csv"))
    write_csv(output / "practices/firm_year_practices_panel.csv", practices, fields(PDATA / "firm_year_practices_panel.csv"))
    report = dict(llm_calls=0, governance=governance, practices=practice_checks)
    if args.figures:
        from plot_figures import replay_figures
        report["figures"] = replay_figures(output / "figures")
    write_json(output / "reproduction_report.json", report)
    summary = dict(output_dir=str(output), llm_calls=0,
                   governance_firm_year_n=governance["firm_year_panel"]["rows"],
                   excluded_firm_year_n=governance["exclusion_panel"]["rows"],
                   practices_firm_year_n=practice_checks["primary_panel"]["rows"],
                   panel_unequal_cells=0)
    if args.figures:
        summary["selected_figures_replayed"] = report["figures"]["selected_figures_replayed"]
        summary["byte_identical_png_n"] = report["figures"]["byte_identical_png_n"]
    print(json.dumps(summary, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
